subtitle: Ushavadata and the Many Roads of Merit

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a grand rock-cut façade with Ushavadata in foreground, hand outstretched toward dark cave mouths and a distant river road
panels.action: Ushavadata stands in ornate Saka attire before a towering rock-cut cave façade, merchants and monks of many robes in the distance, the trade road and river winding away under a hazy western sky.

dialogue.text: In the hills of Karla and Nashik, Ushavadata carved a promise in stone: gifts for monks, Brahmins, travellers and tirthas — without distinction of sect — to bind a new Saka power to many roads of faith.

i18n.hi: कार्ले–नाशिक की पहाड़ियों में उषवदत्त ने पत्थर पर वादा गढ़ा – भिक्षुओं, ब्राह्मणों, यात्रियों और तीर्थों को दान, बिना किसी पंथ भेद के, ताकि नई शक शक्ति कई आस्थाओं से जुड़ जाए।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over the Western Ghats, following a caravan road from the plateau down to the Konkan coast
panels.action: A long line of pack animals and carts snakes along a stone-paved road between steep, forested slopes of the Western Ghats, with glimpses of the distant Arabian Sea beyond.

dialogue.text: In the first centuries of our era, the western coast of India hummed with caravans and ships. Trade from the Deccan and the seas met in the passes of the Ghats, carrying spices, cotton and news.

i18n.hi: युग की शुरुआती सदियों में भारत का पश्चिमी तट कारवाँ और जहाज़ों से गूंजता था। दक्खिन और समुद्र की मंडियाँ घाटों की दर्रों में मिलतीं, मसाले, कपास और खबरें ढोतीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a cliff face pocked with cave mouths above a winding road
panels.action: Rock-cut caves with pillared façades overlook a dusty road; tiny figures of shaven-headed monks and wrapped travellers move between water cisterns carved into the hillside.

dialogue.text: Along these roads, stone hills were hollowed into monasteries and rest-houses. Karla, Nashik, Junnar — caves cut by craftsmen, sustained by merchants, monks and rulers who needed each other.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं रास्तों पर पत्थर की पहाड़ियाँ खोखली कर मठ और सराय बने। कार्ले, नाशिक, जुन्नर – गुफाएँ शिल्पियों के हाथों कटीं, व्यापारियों, भिक्षुओं और राजाओं की आपसी ज़रूरतों से चलती रहीं।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Ushavadata beside a seated Nahapana, with coastal map on a scroll between them
panels.action: Ushavadata, dignified and composed, stands slightly behind an unseen king’s throne, one hand resting near a map showing ports and routes, his jewellery and Saka robe marking his high rank.

dialogue.text: To this world came Ushavadata, son-in-law and chief officer of the Kshaharata ruler Nahapana, a Saka satrap whose authority reached from the coast to the uplands.

i18n.hi: यहीं आया उषवदत्त, क्षहारात शासक नहपान का जामाता और प्रधान अधिकारी, वह शक क्षत्रप जिसकी हुकूमत तट से पठार तक फैली थी।

panels.shot: three-quarter view of Ushavadata inspecting coins and tribute in a hall, flanked by scribes
panels.action: In a pillared hall, Ushavadata watches scribes sort silver coins and tallies on palm-leaf records, his face intent, a blend of calculation and inward resolve.

dialogue.text: His inscriptions call him a great giver, but they also show a careful official. Revenue and power flowed through his hands, and with them the chance to win merit, allies and memory.

i18n.hi: उसके लेख उसे महादानी कहते हैं, पर साथ ही नापतौल करने वाला अफ़सर भी। राजस्व और सत्ता उसकी मुट्ठी से बहते, और साथ ही अवसर – पुण्य, साथी और यादें कमाने का।

panels.shot: wide shot at the base of the Karla cliff, craftsmen and monks around Ushavadata
panels.action: At the base of the Karla hill, artisans with chisels, monks in simple robes and local leaders stand while Ushavadata gestures toward the rock face, as if outlining future halls and rest-houses.

dialogue.speaker: ushavadata
dialogue.text: If the road feeds us, we must shelter the road.

i18n.hi: जो सड़क हमें खिलाए, उसे ही आसरा देना होगा।

panels.shot: low-angle interior wide of Karla’s great chaitya hall under construction
panels.action: Inside a vast rock-cut hall, rough pillars rise toward a vaulted ceiling; scaffolds hold workers while Ushavadata stands in the aisle, dwarfed by the emerging space.

dialogue.text: At Karla he endowed a great cave hall for the Buddhist community, its pillars and roof carved from living rock, its walls later to bear the record of his gifts.

i18n.hi: कार्ले में उसने बौद्ध समाज के लिए विशाल गुफा–सभा बनवाई, जीवित चट्टान से तराशे खंभे और छत, जिनकी दीवारें आगे चलकर उसके दानों का लेखा उठाएंगी।

panels.shot: close-up of a freshly carved inscription panel with Ushavadata watching
panels.action: A stonecutter incises Brahmi letters into a smooth panel in the veranda; Ushavadata watches quietly, hands folded, as the chisel traces the formal words.

dialogue.text: One Karla inscription, cut in clear Brahmi lines, names him: Ushavadata, son of Dinika, son-in-law of Nahapana. It lists his gifts to ascetics in these caves, and then adds a striking pledge.

i18n.hi: कार्ले का एक लेख, साफ़ ब्राह्मी अक्षरों में, उसका नाम देता है – उषवदत्त, दिनिका का पुत्र, नहपान का दामाद। वह इन गुफाओं में तपस्वियों को दिए दान गिनाता है और फिर एक चौंकाने वाली प्रतिज्ञा जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on the inscription panel, without letters visible but clearly central
panels.action: The stone panel fills the frame, its incised lines catching the light, the shapes of letters hinted at but not legible, the rest of the cave blurred beyond.

dialogue.text: He orders that lodgings, food and clothing be given to ascetics staying here — without distinction of sect or origin — binding his name to whoever seeks the cave’s shelter, now or in years ahead.

i18n.hi: वह हुक्म देता है कि यहाँ ठहरने वाले तपस्वियों को रहने, भोजन और वस्त्र मिलें – पंथ और जन्म की बिना किसी छाँट के – ताकि जो भी आज या आने वाले कल में इस गुफा की छाँह मांगे, उसका नाम उससे बँध जाए।

panels.shot: wide interior of the Karla hall showing different ascetics and travellers sharing space
panels.action: Within the completed Karla hall and its side cells, monks in saffron, bare-chested ascetics, and simply dressed travellers sit or rest near water jars and stored grain, the stone ribs arching overhead.

dialogue.text: Later, travellers’ tales and archaeological traces show such caves as shared spaces. Monks chanted, traders rested, wandering holy men paused between tirthas, all beneath a roof linked to his patronage.

i18n.hi: बाद की यात्राओं की कथाएँ और पुरातात्त्विक निशान दिखाते हैं कि ऐसी गुफाएँ साझे ठिकाने थीं। भिक्षु मंत्र जपते, व्यापारी सुस्ताते, घूमंतू साधु तीर्थों के बीच रुकते, सब उस छत के नीचे जो उसकी सरपरस्ती से जुड़ी थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ushavadata presenting gifts to a small group of Brahmins near a sacred fire
panels.action: On a riverbank near a small altar fire, Ushavadata offers a folded cloth and a small pot to seated Brahmins, who receive them with composed faces and uplifted hands.

dialogue.text: But the Karla text is only one piece. Other inscriptions in his name speak of gifts to Brahmins — cows, gold, land and support at sacred places — showing his favour reaching beyond any single path.

i18n.hi: पर कार्ले का लेख अकेला टुकड़ा है। उसके नाम के अन्य शिलालेख ब्राह्मणों को दिए दान बताते हैं – गौदान, स्वर्ण, भूमि और तीर्थस्थानों पर सहायता – दिखाते हैं कि उसकी कृपा एक ही राह तक सीमित नहीं थी।

panels.shot: landscape wide near a tirtha tank, with Ushavadata overseeing the construction of steps and a rest-house
panels.action: Beside a stepped water tank at a pilgrimage spot, workers lay stone blocks while Ushavadata stands slightly apart, looking toward both the tank and a simple shelter being built nearby.

dialogue.text: His records mention tirthas and water works — ponds, embankments, flights of steps — where pilgrims and villagers could drink, bathe and rest, their use quietly joining his name to their journeys.

i18n.hi: उसके लेखों में तीर्थ और जल–व्यवस्थाओं का ज़िक्र है – सरोवर, बाँध, घाट की सीढ़ियाँ – जहाँ तीर्थयात्री और गाँव वाले पी सकें, स्नान कर सकें, विश्राम कर सकें, और इस उपयोग से उनकी यात्राएँ चुपचाप उसके नाम से जुड़ जाएँ।

panels.shot: wide shot of a way-station on a dusty road, with travellers, animals and a stone shelter
panels.action: A stone rest-house stands by a road; travellers with bundles, a weary family and a caravan leader sit in its shade, while Ushavadata rides past on horseback, glancing to ensure its use.

dialogue.text: Nasik cave records speak of provisions for travellers: rest-houses, food and water along the routes. For a satrap whose strength lay on these roads, each shelter was also a thread of loyalty.

i18n.hi: नासिक की गुफाओं के लेख यात्रियों के लिए प्रबंध बताते हैं – सरायें, भोजन और पानी रास्तों पर सजा हुआ। जिन सड़कों से एक क्षत्रप की शक्ति उठती थी, वहाँ हर आसरा वफ़ादारी की एक डोरी भी था।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of a Nasik cave, Ushavadata standing near a simple caitya, inscription panel visible
panels.action: In a smaller Nasik cave, Ushavadata stands near a rock-cut shrine, the quiet interior lit by oil lamps, an inscription panel carved on the wall behind him.

dialogue.text: At Nashik he sponsored cave dwellings for monks, recording his role in detailed formulae. The same hand that aided Brahmins and tirthas also shaped Buddhist refuges above the Godavari valley.

i18n.hi: नाशिक में उसने भिक्षुओं के लिए गुफा–विहार बनवाए, और अपने हिस्से को क़ायदे के शब्दों में दर्ज करवाया। वही हाथ जो ब्राह्मणों और तीर्थों को सहारा दे रहा था, गोदावरी घाटी के ऊपर बौद्ध शरणस्थल भी गढ़ रहा था।

panels.shot: close-up profile of Ushavadata at twilight, looking out over a river and road, face thoughtful
panels.action: Ushavadata stands at the edge of a rock spur at dusk, overlooking a river and a faint line of torches along the road, his profile calm yet intent.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions do not share his inner thoughts. They show acts: gifts scattered across caves, shrines and roads, each gesture blending piety, prestige and the political need to anchor Saka rule.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख उसका मन नहीं खोलते, बस कर्म दिखाते हैं – गुफाओं, देवालयों और सड़कों पर छिटके दान; हर दान में भक्ति, मान–प्रतिष्ठा और शक राज को जड़ें देने की राजनीति गुँथी हुई।

panels.shot: montage wide of carved stones: Karla, Nashik, Junnar, Prabhasa, with weathering and lichen
panels.action: A series of carved stone panels from different sites fills the frame, their edges weathered, some partly covered in lichen, hinting at Karla, Nashik, Junnar and Prabhasa by their distinctive rock.

dialogue.text: From Karla to Nashik, from Junnar to Prabhasa on the western coast, the pattern repeats: a Saka household using wealth to sustain multiple communities at once, leaving its trace in the stone script.

i18n.hi: कार्ले से नाशिक, जुन्नर से पश्चिमी तट के प्रभास तक एक ही ढाँचा उभरता है – एक शक घराना जो एक साथ कई समुदायों को साधने के लिए धन बहाता है, और अपना नाम पत्थर की लिपि में छोड़ जाता है।

panels.shot: historical dissolve from bustling ancient road and cave to a quiet modern archaeological scene
panels.action: The scene shifts from a busy ancient caravan at a cave foot to a modern, empty vista of the same rock-cut façade, now quiet, with a lone figure measuring or sketching.

dialogue.text: Later dynasties would erase Nahapana’s coins and over-inscribe some caves, but archaeologists and epigraphists still teased out Ushavadata’s lines, reading in them a social experiment in patronage.

i18n.hi: आने वाले राजवंशों ने नहपान के सिक्के मिटाए, कुछ गुफाओं पर अपने लेख चढ़ाए, पर पुरातत्त्ववेत्ता और अभिलेख–विद अभी भी उषवदत्त की पंक्तियाँ छाँट पाए, और उनमें संरक्षकता की एक सामाजिक क़ैद आज़माहट पढ़ सके।

panels.shot: low-angle interior of Karla again, with a ghostly overlay of Ushavadata among present-day visitors
panels.action: Modern visitors walk beneath Karla’s stone ribs, while in the same frame a faint, almost translucent Ushavadata stands where his inscription lies, watching the mixed crowd pass.

dialogue.text: Today those caves see tourists, worshippers and scholars of many leanings. The man who once ordered gifts for ascetics of every sect now survives as a name that still shelters differing paths under one carved roof.

i18n.hi: आज उन गुफाओं में तरह–तरह के पर्यटक, उपासक और विद्वान आते हैं। जो आदमी कभी हर पंथ के तपस्वियों के लिए दान लिखवा रहा था, उसका नाम आज भी एक ऐसा छज्जा बना हुआ है, जिसके नीचे अलग–अलग राहें एक ही तराशी छत में आ मिलती हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Ushavadata and the Many Roads of Merit
subtitle_i18n.hi: उषवदत्त और पुण्य की अनेक राहें
